title: Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables
licence: Public university-hosted scan; no explicit reuse licence verified.
why: Supplies the uncited concentration input for independent repeated projection tests. Applying the bounded independent variable inequality to Bernoulli outcomes and to their complements proves the logarithmic dependence on 1/eta for fixed k. This citation supports concentration; the coherent implementation remains the separate deferred-measurement argument in the paper.
source_location: Journal of the American Statistical Association 58 (1963), 13–30. Section 2: Theorem 1, inequality (2.3), printed p15 / PDF page4; Theorem 2, inequality (2.6), printed p16 / PDF page5.
exact_result: For independent Xi in [0,1], P(mean(Xi)−mean(E Xi)>=t)<=exp(−2 n t^2), with the stated range and trivial endpoint extension. Theorem 2 gives P(mean(Xi)−mean(E Xi)>=t)<=exp(−2 n^2 t^2/sum_i (bi−ai)^2) when ai<=Xi<=bi and t>0.
verification_level: Original scan downloaded; theorem statements and hypotheses visually inspected on PDF pages4–5. Full proof not audited in this supplement.
notes: Web PDF extraction contained no usable text; verification used local rendered scan pages. Both iid and nonidentical independent forms are sufficient here; the target's trials are iid for each fixed oracle input. This is a recommended bibliography supplement, not a new proof dependency beyond the standard concentration step already used.

title: The Complexity of Boolean Functions
licence: ECCC landing page states copyright 1987 John Wiley and Sons Ltd and B. G. Teubner; no explicit open reuse licence verified.
why: A precise pedagogical citation for the linear Boolean cost of binary arithmetic used to convert the exact Walsh butterfly computation into a fan-in-two Boolean circuit. The paper should retain the short Walsh recursion argument rather than treating a cyclic DFT theorem as the Walsh result.
source_location: Chapter 3, Section 3.1 Addition and subtraction, Theorem 1.1, printed p40 / PDF page51: school addition has size 5n−3 and depth 2n−1. Subtraction via binary complements is discussed on printed p50 / PDF page61. For related FFT background only: Chapter 3, Section 3.2, Theorem 2.6, printed p64 / PDF page75, states O(n log n) arithmetic size and O(log n) depth for the DFT; proof continues to p65.
exact_result: n-bit binary addition has O(n) size using gates of fan-in at most two. The complement discussion supports the same asymptotic bound for subtraction. Negation and comparison can be implemented with complements/addition and a sign/carry test. For Walsh butterflies, the separate recurrence T(m)=2T(m/2)+m yields m log2(m) additions/subtractions; O_k(log m)-bit arithmetic then yields O_k(m log^2 m) Boolean size.
verification_level: Entire ECCC PDF downloaded and text extracted; relevant theorem, preceding full-adder construction, subtraction discussion, and DFT theorem/proof excerpt inspected. No full-book audit.
notes: The ECCC file is a LaTeX reconstruction of the 1987 book; the landing page explains that numbered items retain their original printed pages. Theorem 2.6 concerns a DFT over suitable rings, not literally the Walsh-Hadamard transform. The arithmetic-to-Boolean application and comparator construction here are elementary derivations, not assertions that Wegener states the target lemma verbatim.
read_status: Entire ECCC PDF downloaded and text extracted; relevant theorem, preceding full-adder construction, subtraction discussion, and DFT theorem/proof excerpt inspected. No full-book audit.

title: Analysis of Boolean Functions (May 2021 arXiv edition)
licence: arXiv licence link explicitly points to CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. PDF front matter also permits single paper or electronic copies for noncommercial personal use and otherwise reserves rights.
why: Optional background for parity characters, Fourier normalization, and orthogonality when reading the Walsh-based forrelation construction. It is not needed as an extra load-bearing result and is not a citation for the butterfly's Boolean gate count.
source_location: Chapter 1, Sections 1.2–1.4: Theorem 1.1 (unique multilinear/Fourier expansion), printed/PDF p22; Definition 1.2 (characters on F2^n), p23; Theorem 1.5 (orthonormal parity basis), p24; Proposition 1.8 and the unnumbered Parseval's Theorem, p25. These locators are for the inspected May 2021 arXiv edition.
exact_result: Every real function on the Boolean cube has a unique multilinear expansion; parity characters form an orthonormal basis under the uniform-average inner product; coefficients are inner products with characters, and Parseval equates the squared norm to the sum of squared Fourier coefficients.
verification_level: Full primary textbook available in web PDF text; front matter and Chapter 1 passages inspected. Not locally downloaded; no full-book audit.
notes: Original book published April 2014. The May 2021 revision corrects 100+ typos/errors, preserves theorem numbering, and changes pagination slightly. Use this edition label with these page locators. Licence link was opened from the arXiv landing page.
